messages:
Maya: FYI — ACME Inc. opened a ticket: private endpoint started failing right after the automated cert rotation at ~10:12. Their app sees: "curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain". Posting minimal repro + logs from the customer below.
Liam (ACME Inc.): our service call to api.private.redwood.example:443 started returning 503s then TLS errors. curl -v shows:
```
> GET /ping HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.private.redwood.example
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate status (22):
* SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```
Liam (ACME Inc.): openssl s_client -connect api.private.redwood.example:443 -servername api.private.redwood.example output:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.private.redwood.example
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = api.private.redwood.example
   i:CN = Acme Internal CA
---
*** No client certificate CA names sent
---
```
Maya: @Harper can you check rotator/rotator-bundle logs? customer says chain only contains leaf; looks like intermediate not served.
eng-ops-bot: cert-rotator job 2027-06-14T17:12:04Z started for tenant acme-inc-private-01
eng-ops-bot: uploaded certificate object cert-tn-8843 (leaf.pem) to lb-binding:lb-az-7
eng-ops-bot: uploaded certificate object cert-tn-8843-chain? NO (fullchain variable empty)
Harper (eng-infra): Investigating — I can repro locally with tenant config that uses a private CA (not LetsEncrypt). It looks like our concatenation step incorrectly handled bundles when intermediate_chain field is present but empty in the rotation API payload. The rotator uploaded leaf.pem only to the NLB, so clients that don't fetch intermediates fail with verify errors.
Harper (eng-infra): Relevant log snippet from rotator (debug):
```
2027-06-14T17:11:58Z rotator: load certs from secret: cert-tn-8843
2027-06-14T17:12:01Z rotator: build_fullchain: intermediates found: 1
2027-06-14T17:12:02Z rotator: concat step returned empty string due to wrong join order
2027-06-14T17:12:03Z rotator: upload leaf.pem -> success
2027-06-14T17:12:04Z rotator: upload fullchain.pem -> skipped (content empty)
```
Maya: Got it. Does this affect only private CA setups or also LetsEncrypt customers?
Harper (eng-infra): Primarily private CA and any bundle where intermediates are provided as an array instead of a single string — our code assumed string and did a noop. We've got a fix on a hotfix branch.
Harper (eng-infra): Immediate mitigation steps I'm executing now: 1) re-generate fullchain concat correctly and push to customer's LB via API; 2) re-trigger bind to reload cert; 3) re-run quick probe.
Harper (eng-infra): Command I'm running internally (API call shown simplified):
```
POST /v1/internal/lb-bindings/lb-az-7/cert
{ "fullchain_pem": "<leaf>\n<intermediate>\n<root?>" }
```
Joe (security): Note: do NOT advise customers to bypass verification. If customer wants a short-term workaround, they can add the intermediate into their JVM truststore or OS trust store. Provide guidance instead of recommending --insecure.
Maya: Sending Liam instructions to update truststore in the short term and telling them we're pushing a hotfix.
Maya -> Liam (ACME Inc.): Could you run this quick check and paste results?
```
# verify server presents fullchain
openssl s_client -connect api.private.redwood.example:443 -servername api.private.redwood.example -showcerts
```
Liam (ACME Inc.): Ran that earlier — it showed only one cert (the leaf). I can add the intermediate to our keystore if needed, but please push the correct chain.
Harper (eng-infra): Hotfix merged to prod branch and deployed to rotator. Re-running rotation for tenant now.
eng-ops-bot: cert-rotator job 2027-06-14T17:32:01Z started for tenant acme-inc-private-01 (retry)
eng-ops-bot: build_fullchain -> success (concatenated 2 certs)
eng-ops-bot: upload fullchain.pem -> success
eng-ops-bot: bind reload -> success (status code 204)
Harper (eng-infra): Ok pushed. Can someone from the customer side re-run the openssl check?
Liam (ACME Inc.): Re-ran openssl s_client now:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Acme Root CA
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = Acme Intermediate CA
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = api.private.redwood.example
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = api.private.redwood.example
   i:C = US, O = Acme Intermediate CA
 1 s:C = US, O = Acme Intermediate CA
   i:C = US, O = Acme Root CA
---
```
Liam (ACME Inc.): Requests now return 200 OK, services back to normal. Thanks.
Maya: Closing the immediate incident, but we should add an integration test for private CA bundle shapes and add a post-rotation probe that validates fullchain on the LB. @Harper can you add a follow-up ticket?
Harper (eng-infra): Yep — creating ENG-ROT-172: add fullchain validation probe + unit test for concat logic. Also will add a health-check that fetches the chain and fails rotation if chain incomplete.
Joe (security): Recommend we run a scan across tenants that rotated yesterday to find any other mis-uploads. I can help with scope.
Maya: Thanks everyone — informing customer and marking support ticket as resolved once we confirm follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
